articles.title: Travis Kelce has a sweet response to Taylor Swift's viral outburst at Arrowhead: “I had to make her proud”
articles.standfirst: Kelce exploded for over 100 yards against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday Night Football.
articles.summary: Kelce exploded for over 100 yards against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday Night Football.
articles.body:
Taylor Swift ’s celebration after Travis Kelce ’s touchdown quickly became one of the defining moments of the Kansas City Chiefs ’ win and now, the NFL star has revealed what he made of his wife’s viral reaction. Swift made her feelings known at Arrowhead Stadium after the 36-year-old tight end found the end zone, as the cameras spied her pointing to her wedding ring and declaring, “That’s my husband!”

The clip quickly went viral across the internet, and the three-time Super Bowl champion addressed it alongside his older brother, Jason , during Wednesday’s episode of their New Heights podcast. “Just doing my deed as a husband,” Travis coolly quipped on September 23 . “Listen man, proud wife, baby. Gotta make my girl proud.” His touchdown was part of a standout night against the Indianapolis Colts , as the Chiefs escaped with a dramatic 33-30 overtime victory to improve to 2-0 for the 2025 NFL season. The score came during a game in which Kelce looked particularly sharp, helping Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs overcome a back-and-forth contest that ultimately went down to the final kick.

Kelce reacts to historic achievement against Colts

Kelce finished with nine catches for 101 yards and that touchdown for one of his best games in recent years, and one that gave him another milestone to celebrate after an eventful night in Kansas City . The veteran also set an NFL record for career receiving yards after the catch, surpassing Marshall Faulk with 6,288 yards after the catch to become the outright leader of any position – including wide receiver. “This is by far the craziest thing and honestly one of the coolest accomplishments I’ve ever had,” Travis continued. “I had no idea I was even in the ballpark. I didn’t know I was Top 5, Top 10, ever. I would have guessed there was so many more. “You don’t get this kind of stuff without having the guys around you to help you get these yards, but at the same time, man, it’s a pretty cool stat to be a part of. “When I’ve got the ball in my hands, I’m doing the most I can with it. It’s proven throughout the history of the NFL that I’ve been pretty good at it.” After Indianapolis and Kansas City traded field goals in overtime, Mahomes connected with Kenneth Walker for a 22-yard completion that put Harrison Butker in position to kick the winning 40-yard field goal. Mahomes threw for 382 yards and three touchdowns, while Walker rushed for 117 yards. Butker then delivered the decisive moment, and critics now wonder if the Chiefs are truly back after finishing with a 6-11 record in 2025.

articles.title: Mahomes' New Weapon: Why Chiefs offense looks unstoppable heading into matchup against the Dolphins
articles.standfirst: The Chiefs’ new backfield threat is creating better conditions for Mahomes and the passing game
articles.summary: The Chiefs’ new backfield threat is creating better conditions for Mahomes and the passing game
articles.body:
Kansas City’s offense has spent years forcing defenses to choose between bad options, but Kenneth Walker III may have added another one.

The Chiefs enter Sunday’s game against the Miami Dolphins at 2-0, and their early-season attack already looks more varied than it did a year ago.

Patrick Mahomes is still the centerpiece, but Walker ’s production through two games has made it much harder for opponents to devote all their attention to the passing game.

Walker has carried 47 times for 290 yards while adding nine receptions, giving Kansas City a runner capable of setting the tempo rather than simply complementing it.

That matters because Miami now has to decide how aggressively it wants to defend the box.

Walker gives Kansas City true early-down weapon

Locked On Chiefs host Chris Clark believes the run game should be central to Kansas City’s plan, with Walker potentially seeing around 20 carries if the game develops that way.

The logic is straightforward. If Miami commits heavier personnel to slowing Walker , Mahomes gets cleaner opportunities against the secondary. If the Dolphins stay light, Walker has already shown he can punish poor tackling and create explosive gains.

Miami has used heavier fronts and base personnel to defend the run, according to Locked On Dolphins host Kyle Crabbs , but that approach creates its own risks against Mahomes and Travis Kelce .

Walker ’s ability to break chunk plays makes the decision even more difficult. He produced four explosive runs in Week 1, including a 60-yard touchdown, and is averaging 6.2 yards per carry through two games.

Chiefs no longer relying on one source

Kansas City’s improvement goes beyond Walker . Kelce has already ripped off a 59-yard reception after topping out at 44 yards on a single catch last season.

Tyquan Thornton made two critical explosive catches against Indianapolis, including a 30-yard gain on third-and-12 in overtime that helped keep the Chiefs alive.

Rashee Rice also delivered four catches for 83 yards in that victory, averaging 20.8 yards per reception. That variety is what makes the offense particularly difficult to prepare for.

Mahomes can attack deep, Walker can control the ground game and Kansas City’s receivers are beginning to generate chunk yardage from several different spots.

Miami cannot afford to let Kansas City dictate game

The Dolphins ’ biggest challenge may be preventing the Chiefs from staying ahead of the chains.

Consistent early-down success would allow Kansas City to mix play-action, quick throws and explosive shots while keeping Miami’s pass rush from controlling the tempo.

Walker has effectively given Mahomes another answer before the ball is even snapped.

Kansas City travels to Hard Rock Stadium on September 27 for its first road game of the season, and Miami will have to solve more than the quarterback who has defined the Chiefs ’ offense for years.

The problem now is that the run game may be just as capable of forcing the defense to adjust.

articles.title: Travis Kelce praises Patrick Mahomes for the way he capitalized on the Colts' coin toss error
articles.standfirst: Mahomes was ready to pounce when the Colts captain appeared to misunderstand the overtime rules
articles.summary: Mahomes was ready to pounce when the Colts captain appeared to misunderstand the overtime rules
articles.body:
Travis Kelce has praised Patrick Mahomes for attempting to turn an unusual coin-toss mistake into a potential advantage during the Kansas City Chiefs’ overtime victory over the Indianapolis Colts.

The bizarre moment unfolded at Arrowhead Stadium after the teams finished regulation tied. Colts safety Camryn Bynum won the overtime coin toss, but instead of choosing to receive or kick, he said he wanted to “defer.”

While that decision is an option at the start of a regular game, it doesn’t apply in overtime because there’s no second half to defer a choice to. The confusion forced referee Craig Wrolstad to pause and clarify exactly what Bynum intended to do.

Mahomes quickly recognized an opportunity. According to Kelce , the Chiefs quarterback told the official that he wanted Kansas City to kick, effectively trying to take advantage of Bynum’s incorrect use of the term “defer.”

Mahomes apparently believed that if the Colts had declined to make a valid choice, the decision would move to Kansas City. He then indicated that the Chiefs wanted to kick and appeared determined to make sure the referee understood his position.

However, the officials didn’t simply accept Mahomes ’ attempt. Wrolstad continued speaking with Bynum and asked additional questions to establish what the Colts actually wanted. Bynum eventually made it clear that Indianapolis wanted to start on defense, meaning the Colts would kick off.

The Chiefs quarterback’s attempt therefore didn’t work, but Kelce was impressed by how quickly Mahomes identified the potential opening.

On the latest episode of New Heights, Kelce explained that Mahomes was completely focused on the situation. He also admitted that he wasn’t entirely familiar with the overtime coin-toss wording himself before his brother Jason Kelce clarified the rule.

“Pat was locked in. ... I don’t even know if defer is something you can say in that situation,” Kelce said.

Kelce explains Mahomes’ quick thinking

Jason Kelce also had plenty to say about the situation, arguing that players chosen as captains should know the coin-toss procedures before stepping into such an important moment. He pointed out that officials have increasingly needed to clarify these decisions because players sometimes use the wrong terminology.

Bynum’s error ultimately didn’t cost the Colts the game. Kansas City still received an opportunity in overtime and eventually won 33-30 when Harrison Butker connected on a 40-yard field goal as time expired.

Mahomes later explained his thinking, saying he believed Bynum’s use of “defer” meant the choice would effectively become Kansas City’s. His strategy wasn’t successful, but it demonstrated how closely he was monitoring every detail during a tense finish.

The episode provided another example of Mahomes ’ instinctive ability to react when an unexpected opportunity presents itself in Kelce’s eyes. The quarterback didn’t need the coin-toss advantage to help Kansas City secure the victory, but he was certainly prepared to capitalize if the rules had allowed it.

The victory moved the Chiefs to 2-0 and gave them an early boost after their 6-11 campaign last season. With Mahomes and Kelce still leading the offense, Kansas City has already shown signs of a different mindset this season, with Kelce previously pointing to improved unity and chemistry within the team.

articles.title: Taylor Swift's new single reveals intimate details about relationship with husband Travis Kelce
articles.standfirst: New song references Kelce’s hometown, their wedding and criticism surrounding their relationship
articles.summary: New song references Kelce’s hometown, their wedding and criticism surrounding their relationship
articles.body:
Taylor Swift has spent years turning the details of her personal life into music, but there is little ambiguity surrounding the inspiration for one of her newest songs.

“Cleveland!,” released Friday as part of The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore, is filled with references to husband Travis Kelce , from his childhood in Cleveland Heights, Ohio, to the couple’s wedding in New York City earlier this summer.

Swift even describes Kelce as the “love of my life,” making the song one of her clearest musical declarations about their relationship since the Kansas City Chiefs star first became part of her public story.

The title itself appears to reference Kelce ’s hometown, while the song also points toward Cleveland Heights and the house where he grew up. Another reference appears to play on New Heights, the podcast Kelce co-hosts with his older brother Jason.

Public criticism turned into part of song

The track doesn't simply celebrate the relationship. Swift also addresses the intense commentary that has followed the couple, including criticism of her personality, their age and whether their romance would last under the scrutiny surrounding two globally recognizable figures.

Rather than treating that attention as a source of uncertainty, the song frames Kelce as the person whose opinion ultimately matters. That theme reaches its clearest point when Swift calls him the “love of my life.”

The ending adds another apparent nod to their July 3 wedding at Madison Square Garden, with Swift singing, “Now I’m wearing white!” The couple married less than three months before the new material arrived.

Growing catalog of Kelce-inspired songs

Swift has previously been linked to Kelce through songs including “The Alchemy” and “So High School” on The Tortured Poets Department, before their relationship appeared to influence several tracks on The Life of a Showgirl.

Those included “Elizabeth Taylor,” “Opalite” and “Wood.” Swift later acknowledged during an appearance with Jimmy Fallon that “Wood” had evolved significantly from its original concept.

“I brought this into the studio and I was like I wanna do a throwback, kind of timeless-sounding song,” Swift said. “It really started out in a very innocent place… I don’t know what happened, man.”

Four new songs expand ‘The Life of a Showgirl’

“Cleveland!” arrives alongside three other new tracks: “Patient Zero,” “Pink Clouding” and “Babylon.”

Swift wrote and produced the material in Sweden with longtime collaborators Max Martin and Shellback , describing the songs as being created out of gratitude for the response to The Life of a Showgirl.

The release also comes shortly before Swift ’s appearance at the MTV Video Music Awards, where she is expected to debut the “Patient Zero” music video. Kelce , though, gets perhaps the most personal moment of the new collection.

Between Cleveland, his childhood home, their marriage and Swift ’s declaration of love, “Cleveland!” leaves considerably less room for fan detective work than many of her previous songs.

articles.title: Who was Lamar Hunt, Clark Hunt's father, and how did his legacy change Chiefs history?
articles.standfirst: The Chiefs founder helped create the AFL and moved the team to Kansas City
articles.summary: The Chiefs founder helped create the AFL and moved the team to Kansas City
articles.body:
Long before the Kansas City Chiefs became one of the NFL’s defining franchises, Lamar Hunt was trying to force his way into professional football.

Unable to secure an NFL franchise, Hunt helped establish the American Football League in 1959 and launched the Dallas Texans as one of its original teams. Four years later, he moved the franchise to Kansas City and renamed it the Chiefs .

The AFL-NFL merger in 1970 eventually transformed the sport, and Hunt ’s influence became permanent enough that the AFC Championship trophy now bears his name.

Clark Hunt , however, has often described a very different side of the man remembered as a football pioneer.

“My dad was a great father,” Clark said in a 2013 interview with the Chiefs.

Father led through example

Lamar ’s business reputation was built on bold decisions, but Clark remembers a leadership style that was much quieter.

“He was somebody who led by example,” Clark said. “More so than somebody who was prone to giving lectures, but it would be to treat others as you would want to be treated.”

That philosophy became especially important after Lamar died in December 2006 and Clark took on a larger leadership role with the organization.

Clark has said one of the clearest lessons involved the way Lamar thought about supporters.

“The fans were always his focus,” Clark said. He recalled his father repeatedly asking, “How’s this going to benefit our fans? How’s this going to make the experience at Arrowhead better on Sunday?”

Clark added: “Our fans are the lifeblood of the organization; that’s really a lesson that he taught me.”

Lamar Hunt’s sporting legacy

Kansas City remains the most visible expression of Hunt ’s influence, but his impact stretched well beyond the NFL.

He was also deeply involved in professional soccer in the United States and played a role in bringing the 1994 FIFA World Cup to the country.

That wider sporting vision helped establish Hunt as one of the most influential owners of his era, but Clark has repeatedly emphasized that his father’s legacy was never just about expansion, trophies or business success.

It was also about how people were treated and what kind of institution the family wanted to build.

Personal memories had little to do with football

One of Clark ’s favorite stories about his father involves the annual Turkey Trot in Dallas.

“It was something he and I started when I was about seven years old,” Clark said.

The tradition began after Clark suffered an injury and Lamar decided they would run an eight-mile race together despite neither being prepared for the distance.

“I can’t say I necessarily looked forward to it every year,” Clark said, “but it’s definitely a special memory of something he and I did.”

That story helps explain why Lamar Hunt ’s influence remains so central to Clark ’s stewardship of the Chiefs .

His father helped build a league, moved a franchise and changed the structure of professional football.

Clark ’s task has been different: preserve the values behind it while allowing the organization to evolve.

articles.title: Travis Kelce calls on the NFL to address dangerous field conditions after ‘Squirt Squad’ moment shocks him
articles.standfirst: Travis and Jason were surprised by how hot it was at the Titans' stadium last week
articles.summary: Travis and Jason were surprised by how hot it was at the Titans' stadium last week
articles.body:
With a 2-0 start and more than 30 points in both games, you can say the Kansas City Chiefs have already put last year’s slip behind them, that 6-11 mark that was the franchise’s worst since 2012 (2-14) and the worst of the Andy Reid era , only the second time in 13 seasons as head coach he missed the playoffs.

Bringing in Kenneth Walker III , the league’s leading rusher, and putting Eric Bieniemy back as offensive coordinator has been a big part of why this start looks different, and Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce look as sharp as they did in those early years together.

Best example was the 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts , when Mahomes threw for 382 yards , his highest single-game passing total since 2023, and Kelce went for nine catches, 101 yards and a touchdown, his best game since 2024.

Travis Kelce Calls Out Extreme Heat on NFL Turf

Next up are the Miami Dolphins in one of the hottest buildings in the NFL, and the one break for Kansas City, especially for Kelce, is that Hard Rock Stadium is natural grass, not artificial turf.

That matters after the last episode of New Heights , when Kelce reacted to video of coaches spraying water straight onto players’ shoes to fight the heat. “The squirt squad was out there! What is this?” he said. “You shouldn’t be allowed to do that. You shouldn’t be allowed to put players on a field that does that. Why is that even allowed?”

That was after the turf at Nissan Stadium hit 157 degrees Fahrenheit during the game, up from 95 at kickoff, heat that reportedly melted the soles of cleats and forced emergency measures on the sideline.

“It’s so insane to me that you’re allowed to put the product in a situation like that. The NFL has got to figure something out for that. That’s insane.”

Nissan is one of 14 NFL venues still on artificial turf , and 16 of the league’s 32 teams play home games on synthetic surfaces, including outdoor stadiums used by the Patriots, Seahawks, Bengals, Giants and Jets.

NFLPA Keeps Pushing Grass After Injury Numbers

Kelce was not the only one. Eagles tackle Jordan Mailata , who has sat in those talks for the NFL Players Association , tied it back to the union’s long push for natural grass in every stadium.

The NFLPA has pointed to 2012-2018 data showing a 28% higher rate of non-contact lower-extremity injuries on turf than grass , including 32% more non-contact knee injuries and 69% more non-contact foot and ankle injuries.

The league’s answer is that overall injury rates look similar when you count every category, and they have used 2025 numbers of 0.43 injuries per game on turf versus 0.42 on grass .

That is the fight sitting in the background while the Chiefs fly to Miami 2-0, with Mahomes and Kelce rolling and a grass field waiting instead of another 157-degree track.

“It’s so insane to me that you’re allowed to put the product in a situation like that. The NFL has got to figure something out for that. That’s insane.”

Nissan is one of 14 NFL venues still on artificial turf , and 16 of the league’s 32 teams play home games on synthetic surfaces, including outdoor stadiums used by the Patriots, Seahawks, Bengals, Giants and Jets.
NFLPA Keeps Pushing Grass After Injury Numbers
Kelce was not the only one. Eagles tackle Jordan Mailata , who has sat in those talks for the NFL Players Association , tied it back to the union’s long push for natural grass in every stadium.

The NFLPA has pointed to 2012-2018 data showing a 28% higher rate of non-contact lower-extremity injuries on turf than grass , including 32% more non-contact knee injuries and 69% more non-contact foot and ankle injuries.
The league’s answer is that overall injury rates look similar when you count every category, and they have used 2025 numbers of 0.43 injuries per game on turf versus 0.42 on grass .
That is the fight sitting in the background while the Chiefs fly to Miami 2-0, with Mahomes and Kelce rolling and a grass field waiting instead of another 157-degree track.

articles.title: FOX reporter Erin Andrews' gift to Brittany Mahomes shows that their relationship is going very well
articles.standfirst: Erin Andrews’ latest gesture highlights her longstanding friendship with Brittany Mahomes
articles.summary: Erin Andrews’ latest gesture highlights her longstanding friendship with Brittany Mahomes
articles.body:
Erin Andrews appears to have given Brittany Mahomes another reason to look forward to the next Kansas City Chiefs game.

The FOX Sports broadcaster and WEAR by Erin Andrews founder recently sent Mahomes a collection of Chiefs-themed clothing, and Brittany responded with a short but appreciative message on Instagram. She shared a glimpse of the package and tagged both Andrews and her fashion brand, writing, “Thank you.”

The thoughtful gift reportedly featured a wide selection of Chiefs merchandise, including tees, hoodies, tanks, windbreakers, jackets and accessories. That gives Brittany plenty of options for her next game-day appearance.

Andrews was quick to respond after seeing Brittany’s post. She reposted the Instagram story and added a series of heart emojis alongside “U!!”

Brittany has previously supported Andrews ’ brand by wearing WEAR pieces on game days and thanking the FOX Sports personality for sending merchandise. Their support hasn’t been one-sided, either.

Brittany has also sent Andrews gifts, including a game-day bundle from Divi, the Dallas-based hair-care company for which she’s a brand ambassador.

Erin Andrews’ WEAR continues to make waves around the Chiefs

Andrews launched WEAR with Constance Schwartz-Morini in 2019 after noticing a gap in the market for fashionable sports apparel aimed at women. The brand has since expanded across several major sports and leagues, including the NFL, MLB, NHL, NBA, WNBA, NCAA, WWE and U.S. Soccer.

WEAR has also developed a notable connection with the Chiefs through Taylor Swift. Swift attended Kansas City’s Week 2 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts on September 20 and was spotted wearing a Chiefs tank from Andrews’ collection. The $39.99 piece attracted significant attention and sold out soon afterward.

Swift has worn WEAR apparel before, including during the 2025 Super Bowl, helping bring additional attention to Andrews ’ growing sports-fashion business.

Andrews ’ latest package arrives during an eventful start to the 2026 NFL season for Brittany . Kansas City improved to 2-0 after defeating Indianapolis 33-30 in overtime.

Patrick Mahomes delivered a huge performance, completing 32 of 47 passes for 382 yards and three touchdowns. Harrison Butker ultimately sealed the victory with a 40-yard field goal as time expired.

Brittany also admitted that the dramatic contest got the better of her emotions. Following the victory, she apologized on Instagram for screaming and using “a lot of bad words” during the game.

Patrick Mahomes , meanwhile, has emphasized that the Chiefs can’t afford to become complacent after their unbeaten opening. With Miami next on the schedule, Brittany could soon have another opportunity to show off her latest WEAR collection from Andrews .

articles.title: Chris Jones' lingering issue could hurt Patrick Mahomes' plans for Week 3
articles.standfirst: Kansas City could be without a key defensive presence as Chris Jones continues to deal with a calf issue
articles.summary: Kansas City could be without a key defensive presence as Chris Jones continues to deal with a calf issue
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs enter their Week 3 meeting with the Miami Dolphins carrying a few injury concerns, with Chris Jones' continued limitations standing out as one of the biggest.

Kansas City is 2-0 and will look to maintain its perfect start in Miami, but the status of several defensive players could affect how the game unfolds.

Jones has been dealing with a calf injury since Week 1 and remained a limited participant in practice. The veteran defensive tackle also played through the problem last week, meaning his ability to handle a full workload on Sunday remains something to monitor.

His absence would create a significant challenge for Kansas City. Jones remains one of the most experienced and productive pieces of the Chiefs' defensive front, and losing him could put additional pressure on the rest of the unit.

While the latest reports haven't ruled him out, the recurring limitation suggests the team is still managing the injury carefully.

The Chiefs have encouraging developments elsewhere. Chamarri Conner has returned to limited work after missing time following a training camp collision, while rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has progressed to full participation.

Jaden Hicks has also been heavily involved, giving Kansas City more options in a secondary that has dealt with injuries.

L'Jarius Sneed, meanwhile, remains limited because of his knee. Kansas City has continued to manage his practice workload, but he's been available on game day. Patrick Mahomes has also been able to practice fully, providing some positive news for the Chiefs' offense.

Chiefs balancing injuries with Walker's workload

Josh Simmons remains another concern. The left tackle has continued to miss practice because of his back injury and hasn't been able to reclaim his expected starting role. That leaves Kansas City relying on its replacement while Simmons ' return timetable remains uncertain.

The Chiefs are also planning to manage Kenneth Walker III's workload. Walker has been a major part of the team's 2-0 start, producing significant all-purpose yardage while handling a heavy number of touches.

Kansas City doesn't want to take him out of the offensive equation, but the coaching staff wants to give rookie Emmett Johnson more opportunities.

That approach could help preserve Walker's effectiveness as the season progresses while allowing Johnson to develop. The rookie has already shown enough to earn additional opportunities, giving the Chiefs another option for keeping their running game productive without relying exclusively on Walker .

The central concern for the Chiefs heading into Miami is whether Kansas City can keep its key players healthy. Jones ' calf remains the biggest defensive question, while Simmons ' absence continues to affect the offensive line.

With the Chiefs chasing a third straight victory, Sunday's matchup should provide another indication of how well they can manage those lingering issues.
